channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Samarkand Conference Focuses on Youth Rights, Digital Space, and Climate Change
item.description: The XII World Conference of Young Parliamentarians in Samarkand featured panel discussions on youth rights amid conflicts, digital rights in the digital age, and climate change. Discussions included protecting youth rights, ensuring educational opportunities, and addressing online security challenges. International cooperation was emphasized for supporting youth in conflict zones and improving legislative mechanisms.

item.title: Samarkand Conference Ideas Aim to Strengthen International Cooperation
item.description: The XII World Conference of Young Parliamentarians in Samarkand, initiated by Uzbekistan's President, is seen as recognition of the country's progress in parliamentarism and youth policy. The conference theme focuses on human dignity, justice, and peace amid instability. Participants emphasized constructive dialogue, mutual trust, and partnership, calling for youth involvement in decision-making.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Fines for Concealing Offenses, Including Early Marriages
item.description: Uzbekistan's Prosecutor General's Office has drafted a bill introducing administrative liability for failing to report offenses. The proposed amendments to the Code of Administrative Offenses would penalize officials and citizens who do not report violations to the authorities. Fines would range from 3 to 15 BHM depending on the offense and repeat violations.

item.title: Chairwoman of the Senate Outlines Three Priority Directions
item.description: At the XII World Conference of Young Parliamentarians in Samarkand, it was highlighted that Uzbekistan's population is nearly 39 million, with over half under 30. The Senate Chairwoman stated that youth policy is integral to national development and reforms, with constitutional guarantees and the "Uzbekistan-2030" strategy prioritizing youth interests in education, employment, and social protection.

item.title: System for Training Medical and Pharmaceutical Personnel to Be Improved
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed proposals to enhance the training, registration, and continuous professional development of medical and pharmaceutical personnel. The reforms aim to shift medical education from theory to practical skills, align programs with international standards, and create a system for objective assessment and career growth, with admission quotas based on regional needs and staff shortages.

item.title: Youth participation in decision-making and human rights protection emphasized at Samarkand conference
item.description: The XII World Conference of Young Parliamentarians in Samarkand highlighted the growing role of youth in international decision-making. Speakers stressed the importance of dialogue and cooperation among young parliamentarians to address global challenges. Concerns were raised about the regression in human rights protection and the need for parliaments to firmly defend basic rights.

item.title: Global Food Prices Reach Highest Level Since Late 2022 in August
item.description: Global food prices surged in August, reaching their highest point since the end of 2022. Price indices for vegetable oil, sugar, meat, and dairy products all increased. The cereal price index rose by 2.2% over the month, hitting its highest level since May 2024.

item.title: US Senator Steve Daines praises Uzbekistan's stable development and regional role
item.description: Uzbekistan's First Deputy Chairman of the Senate, Sodik Safoyev, met with US Senator Steve Daines. They discussed strengthening Uzbek-American strategic partnership, inter-parliamentary ties, and regional cooperation. Senator Daines highly praised Uzbekistan's reforms and stable development, emphasizing its key role in regional cooperation and the development of the Middle Corridor.

item.title: UN Youth Envoy Felipe Paullier Highlights Samarkand as Platform for Youth Action
item.description: Felipe Paullier, UN Assistant Secretary-General for Youth Affairs, praised the XII Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians in Samarkand. He stated that such forums are crucial for strengthening UN principles and that Samarkand has become an important platform encouraging youth to take practical action and participate in decision-making.

item.title: Central Asian Youth Discuss Climate Change and Water Security at Regional Conference in Samarkand
item.description: The Third Regional Conference of Youth RCOY Central Asia 2026, themed 'Central Asian Youth for Water Security and Climate Justice,' has commenced in Samarkand. Over 100 young activists and experts from various Central Asian countries and beyond are participating to discuss climate change impacts, water management, and regional policy.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Taxi Market Evolution Since Early 2026 Detailed
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Tax Committee reported on the taxi market from January to August 2026. Over 242 taxi aggregators are integrated into tax systems, facilitating 329 million passenger trips. Total revenue exceeded 7.2 trillion soms, with non-cash payments comprising 36.9%.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Compares Engineering Survey Methods with International Standards
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Department of Engineering Surveys is comparing domestic engineering-geological survey methods with international practices. Tests were conducted in Bishkek using Kyrgyz and Chinese methodologies. The goal is to evaluate efficiency and potential adoption of various techniques.

item.title: Uzbek MP Notes Increased Critical Analysis and Bold Judgments in Media
item.description: Odiljon Tojiyev, a member of the Legislative Chamber and head of the National Association of Mass Media, observes a rise in bold opinions, critical perspectives, and deep analysis within Uzbekistan's media landscape. He emphasizes journalism's role in public control and addressing citizen needs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ministry of Health and UNFPA Discuss Cervical Cancer Screening Program
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Health and the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) have discussed the implementation of HPV DNA testing and the development of a cervical cancer screening program. Key areas of cooperation in reproductive health were addressed.

item.title: Uzbekistan's SCO Initiatives in Bishkek Lay Foundation for Eurasian Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan presented initiatives at the SCO summit in Bishkek, proposing the 'SCO-2040: Space of Common Development' concept. This strategy shifts the SCO's focus from security to development, aiming to create a platform for investment, technology, and infrastructure projects across Eurasia.

item.title: Tashkent City Khokimiyat Reports Elimination of Unpleasant Odor from Salar Wastewater Treatment Plant
item.description: Tashkent's Salar wastewater treatment plant has installed new filtration equipment costing 9.5 billion soms to eliminate unpleasant odors. The city administration reports that sealed reservoirs and special filters are now in use, resolving the issue.

item.title: Uzbekistan and UNICEF to Enhance Social Protection Mechanisms Against Risks
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Economy and Finance met with UNICEF to develop an adaptive social protection strategy. This strategy will improve citizen support measures considering climate, natural, and economic risks, strengthening household resilience and expanding access to social assistance.

item.title: Young Parliamentarians Aim to Realize Human Rights, Not Just Declarations
item.description: Hasan Ibrahim highlighted the urgency of restoring human rights amidst global crises at the World Conference of Young Parliamentarians. He emphasized that hope is linked to secured rights, urging young parliamentarians to transform rights from mere declarations into tangible realities for a better future.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's first car plant linked to presidential affairs chief's sister
item.description: An investigation by Temirov Live reveals that the sister of the head of the presidential affairs administration, Kanybek Tumanbaev, is repeatedly implicated in the country's first car plant. The administration itself is also involved in the project.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes state registration for medical and pharmaceutical staff from 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan is proposing to implement state registration for medical and pharmaceutical personnel starting in 2030. Professionals not registered by then will not be permitted to practice medicine or pharmacy. A dedicated center will be established to manage this process.

item.title: Tanzila Narbaeva: Youth Are a Force Capable of Influencing Global Processes
item.description: Speaking at the XII World Conference of Young Parliamentarians in Samarkand, Tanzila Narbaeva emphasized youth's active role. She stated that the President's message highlighted Uzbekistan's commitment to supporting youth engagement and parliamentary diplomacy. Narbaeva believes young politicians bring new ideas and responsibility for the future, crucial for dialogue in unstable times.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Rostov Region Discuss Interregional Cooperation and Citizen Rights
item.description: A delegation from Uzbekistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs met with Rostov region officials to discuss expanding trade, economic, and investment cooperation. They also focused on labor mobility for Uzbek citizens and improving procedures for work permits. An agreement was reached to hold a meeting with the regional Interior Ministry to simplify patent acquisition.

item.title: New production zone to be established on land transferred from Uzbekistan to Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A new production zone will be built on 105 hectares of land transferred from Uzbekistan to Kyrgyzstan, according to the Osh mayor's office. Officials inspected the site suitable for industrial facilities. The land transfer was formalized through agreements signed in late 2022 and ratified in early 2023.

item.title: Plague outbreak activity confirmed in Mongolian region bordering Russia
item.description: High epizootic activity of a natural plague focus has been recorded in a region of Mongolia bordering Russia. Specialists' conclusions are based on laboratory research conducted in 2026. The affected area is the transboundary Sailugem focus, covering approximately 29,000 square kilometers.

item.title: Samarkand hosts World Conference of Young Parliamentarians on human rights and justice
item.description: The XII World Conference of Young Parliamentarians is underway in Samarkand, focusing on ensuring human rights, dignity, and justice amid instability. Over 250 young parliamentarians from nearly 60 countries and representatives from 11 international organizations are participating. The event aims to enhance youth participation in public life and parliamentary activities.

item.title: Former Uzbek soldier serving as drone operator in Russian army sentenced in Russia
item.description: A former Uzbek soldier, who served as a drone operator in the Russian Armed Forces, has been sentenced to over 11 years in prison in Russia for drug-related crimes. He claims he was deceived into joining the war in Ukraine, where he operated surveillance drones and relayed information about Ukrainian positions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan launches new plant for apple processing
item.description: A new Global ECO Green plant in Kyrgyzstan's Ala-Buka district will process apples, including unsaleable, unassorted, and undersized fruit, starting October 1. The facility will produce natural apple concentrate for domestic and export markets, with a capacity to process up to 45,000 tons of apples per season.

item.title: Tajikistan's Migration Agency Invites Citizens to Work in Japan with Salaries Above $2,800
item.description: Tajikistan's Agency for Work and Migration Abroad has announced job opportunities in Japan for Tajik citizens. The agency reported that potential earnings for these positions exceed $2,800 per month, encouraging job seekers to apply.

item.title: New Seven-Story Complex for 'Kyzmat' State Institution Under Construction Near Bishkek Arena
item.description: A new seven-story complex for the state institution 'Kyzmat' is being built near 'Bishkek Arena' and is expected to open in a few months. The facility will house public service centers, staff offices, and a multi-level parking lot.

item.title: New Government Service Center 'Kyzmat' Under Construction Near Bishkek Arena
item.description: A new seven-story complex for the state institution 'Kyzmat' is being built near 'Bishkek Arena' and is expected to open in a few months. The center will house public service centers (PSCs) on the first two floors, a personalization center and archive on the third and fourth, and offices for staff and management on upper floors. It will also feature a multi-level parking lot.

item.title: Opposition Figure Tilekmat Kurenov Denies Inciting Power Seizure
item.description: Opposition figure Tilekmat Kurenov stated he did not call for a seizure of power after his court hearing was postponed. The session was rescheduled to September 11 due to the absence of his lawyer.

item.title: Uzbekistan's evolving view of Central Asia in its foreign policy discourse
item.description: Uzbekistan has shifted its perspective on Central Asia multiple times over 35 years, exploring integration and later including Afghanistan. The current foreign policy concept, from 2012, prioritizes the region but lacks a clear definition, leading to debates about expanding regional dialogue formats.

item.title: New facilities opened in Panj district, Tajikistan, ahead of Independence Day
item.description: Several new facilities, including an additional school building and a teahouse, were opened in Tajikistan's Panj district on September 3, 2026, coinciding with the 35th anniversary of the country's independence. The school expansion will accommodate 200 students, and the teahouse will create 12 jobs.

item.title: Joint Venture to Oversee Construction of Nuclear Power Plant in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to establish a joint venture to manage the construction of its first integrated nuclear power plant in the Jizzakh region. The project aims to employ over 10,000 workers, with 65-70% being local personnel. Construction of the first power unit's foundation is underway, with significant concrete poured.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Discusses Fuel and Lubricant Supply Stability
item.description: A meeting chaired by Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers Erlist Akunbekov addressed the supply of fuel and lubricants to Kyrgyzstan. Representatives from the Ministry of Energy, ABank, and petroleum product suppliers discussed market conditions and measures for stable supply. Instructions were given to relevant state agencies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan discusses fuel and lubricant supply with energy ministry and banks
item.description: A meeting chaired by Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers addressed fuel and lubricant supply for the population and economy. Participants from the Ministry of Energy, ABank, and petroleum companies discussed market conditions and stable supply measures. No forecasts for fuel price increases were announced, with officials stating it depends on the market.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes law to dismiss police inspectors if over 50% of residents express distrust
item.description: A draft law in Uzbekistan aims to establish the status, duties, and social protections for preventive police inspectors. Introduced by the President, the bill passed its first reading in the Legislative Chamber. It proposes dismissing inspectors if more than 50% of residents in their district express distrust.

item.title: Criminal case opened after explosion on Glinka Street in Tashkent
item.description: Tashkent authorities have opened a criminal case following an explosion on Glinka Street that damaged the road surface. Preliminary findings suggest a gas leak from an underground pipeline in a utility chamber caused the incident. Investigations are ongoing to determine the exact cause and assign legal responsibility.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's fuel and lubricant supply discussed by cabinet
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's cabinet held a meeting to discuss the supply of fuel and lubricants to the country's population and economy. Participants reviewed the current market situation and stable supply issues. No forecasts for fuel price increases were provided, with officials stating it depends on the market.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's government discusses fuel and lubricant supply
item.description: A meeting chaired by Deputy Head of the Cabinet of Ministers Erlist Akunbekov addressed the stable supply of fuel and lubricants to Kyrgyzstan's population and economy. Participants discussed the current market situation and received relevant instructions. No forecasts for price increases are currently available, with future prices depending on market dynamics.
